description:
Replace the source-text substring cutover guard with a compile-time visibility restriction so only the mutation-session API can publish into repository roots, retaining the deleted-module and renderer-owner assertions.

## Background

The current cutover guard is the substring test at `crates/jit/tests/provenance_contract/repository_state_cutover_tests.rs:39-67`. It greps the production halves of the four cutover command modules for ~14 forbidden substrings (for example `"std::fs::write("`, `"OpenOptions::new("`, `"atomic_write"`), splitting production from test source on the literal `"\n#[cfg(test)]\nmod "`. This enforces the narrative, not a property: it breaks on reformatting and is defeated by moving a raw write one file over. The property it approximates is that only the mutation-session API may publish into repository roots.

The visibility replacement makes that property compiler-enforced:

- `FileTransactionKernel` (and `TransactionControlLocation`) and the in-repository writers `write_file_atomic` / `write_file_atomic_bytes` tighten from `pub(crate)` to `pub(in crate::storage)`. Their only callers -- `repository_state_store.rs`, `user_config_store.rs`, `file_transaction.rs` -- live in `crate::storage`, so repository-owned publishers compile unchanged while `crate::commands` can no longer name them.
- The three external-export wrappers `write_external_export_atomic`, `publish_external_file_noreplace`, and `publish_external_directory_noreplace` move into a new `storage::external_publish` submodule re-exported `pub(crate)`. Their legitimate callers `commands/snapshot.rs` and `commands/graph.rs` publish to caller-chosen paths outside repository roots (charter D-4), and the module name states that intent.
- The low-level rename primitive `rename_noreplace_cap` is a repository transaction primitive, not an export API: it stays `pub(in crate::storage)` alongside the in-repository writers, reachable by the external-publish wrappers only through their storage-internal implementation.

Residual raw `std::fs` publishing cannot be restricted by visibility, so one narrow assertion is retained in the same provenance-contract suite: it scans **only** the four cutover command modules for the four raw `std::fs` publisher calls (`fs::write`, `fs::rename`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions::new`). This is a deliberate, recorded exception to the visibility mechanism. A crate-wide `clippy.toml` disallowed-methods rule is rejected because `commands/snapshot.rs` legitimately stages exports with raw `std::fs` into temp directories.

The deleted-module and renderer-owner tests in the same file (`:69-139` and `:141-161`) are retained verbatim; only the substring test is deleted.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The cutover guard enforces publisher visibility (`pub(in crate::storage)` on `FileTransactionKernel`, `TransactionControlLocation`, `write_file_atomic`, `write_file_atomic_bytes`, and `rename_noreplace_cap`; external-export wrappers relocated to a `pub(crate)` `storage::external_publish` submodule) instead of source-text substring matching, and the substring test is removed.
- [hard] REQ-02: The deleted-module and renderer-owner assertions in the provenance-contract suite are retained unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: `crate::commands` cannot name the tightened publishers (the build fails if it does), while `repository_state_store.rs`, `user_config_store.rs`, `file_transaction.rs`, `commands/snapshot.rs`, and `commands/graph.rs` compile against their permitted surfaces unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-04: One narrow assertion remains in the provenance-contract suite scanning only the four cutover command modules for the four raw `std::fs` publisher calls (`fs::write`, `fs::rename`, `File::create`, `OpenOptions::new`).

## Notes

Do not introduce a crate-wide `clippy.toml` disallowed-methods rule; `commands/snapshot.rs` uses raw `std::fs` legitimately for temp-directory export staging. The suite must not add any integration-test target.
title: Visibility-enforced cutover guard
